module_correspondence.conclusion: The four adjacent-pair generators on five bits span exactly the parity-zero vectors; their check equations force a constant vector. The finite domains are genuinely all 32 vectors and all 16 coefficient lists. The odd length five gives constant parity t and single-basis parity 1. Independent bit enumeration reproduces the full local span/kernel facts.

The 25 physical qubits are Fin5 x Fin5. X checks cover two adjacent whole five-qubit blocks; Z checks cover adjacent coordinate pairs within one block. Their overlaps are zero or two, giving actual orthogonality. X_rowspace and Z_rowspace prove the exact descriptions, and centralizer_iff is derived from actual full generator tests, not assumed.

For every centralizer Pauli, X is constant on each five-qubit block and Z block parities are equal. If any constant X block is nonzero, its five distinct coordinates inject into total union support. Otherwise X=0; being outside the stabilizer forces nonzero common Z parity, giving a supported coordinate in each of five distinct blocks. This covers all mixed X/Z labels. The X-only single-block witness has odd block-value parity, is outside the actual stabilizer and has support five. quantum_distance_five follows with both directions.

The actual family matrices are diagonal copies of the same Shor X/Z matrices. diagonal_synth and diagonal_rowspace prove full rowspace decomposition; stabilizer_blocks and centralizer_blocks prove exact generated-stabilizer and full symplectic-orthogonal decomposition. A global logical label has a logical component by contraposition of the proved stabilizer identity. block_weight_le injects component support into total support. Supported witnesses are logical and have exact weight five. These prove exact distance five for every m>0, without assuming the key block bridge.

combinedCheck includes both X and Z rows of the SAME code. tanner is their actual symmetric loopless bipartite incidence SimpleGraph against physical qubits. Two X checks in the first copy share block 1; two distinct coordinates there give the displayed genuine four-cycle. IsCycle uses a proved tail path and length four. Bipartite incidence excludes three-step closed walks; simplicity and Mathlib's cyclic-girth lower bound exclude shorter cycles. The actual shortest-cycle argument gives girth_four for every m>0.

rowDegree_card and colDegree_card identify the counters with actual incidence support cardinalities. Seed X rows have weight 10, Z rows weight 2, and each qubit has at most two X plus two Z checks. Diagonal row/column identities preserve these actual combined bounds, proving row<=10 and col<=4 for every m. qubit_card is 25m and unbounded_length uses positive m=n+1. All bounds and distance/graph objects share the same Code definitions.

IsLDPCFamily explicitly requires uniform row/column bounds and unbounded qubit cardinality. familyCode n=code(n+1) has no zero-block member, and isLDPCFamily, family_distance and family_girth establish admissibility and exact values. The constructed sequence in fact grows linearly, not only along a sparse subsequence.

UniversalBound is the necessary family consequence of the source's universal CSS LDPC inequality: every member with an attained quantum distance must obey d/g<=L(g)/2. refute_bound instantiates it on this actual admissible family at its real distance 5 and real Tanner girth 4. The arithmetic contradiction 5/4>1 is then on these proved source objects, not substituted input numbers.

log_four proves ln4=2ln2. The established ln2 bound supplies L(4)<=2 for natural log. For b>=2, ln(b)>=ln2>0, so the proved logb definition and division inequality give log_b4<=2.
